tips.comment: Prospect House has won twice over two miles one furlong here since being fitted with a visor and only up six pounds for the two wins he might gain a third win over two furlongs further with William Maggs riding again.

This looks winnable for an improver and both Camino Rocio and Climbing have lost form chasing and have been switched back to hurdling and Tennessee Orange only won a small field point over two and a half miles. Ex Irish Jullou De Grissay has so far not done much in Irish hurdle races and the two points he won were fairly weak, his latest run over hurdles at Warwick was against decent opposition and it was not unexpected to be a distant 3rd but he is not out of this race at 9-1 outsider.

Zoffalee has had two runs back since a lengthy 2 year break and has progressed without being asked to do too much. Was behind Big Bee Hive last time and was going well before fitness told on the run and the rider was not hard on him. Now on a very good mark and in sound shape the big question is likely to be asked today. Conditions are optimum and can be backed EW with a degree of confidence at 12/1.

Taking a chance on the 3 places with B365 holding up, (7 runners) & the wind-op continuing
 to work on her third run. On her third last time over CD 18 days ago, Mike Sowersby's 6yo is closely weighted with 2nd favourite Game Beaaa & she's well handicapped on her Irish form from last year.
She's got bottle a good horse on the flat not showed anything yet over hurdles but this is a weak looking race and it has been well backed so worth the risk

He's back on the same mark he ran off in this same race last season. Coming into this off the back of a decent run lto. 
As mentioned above. He ran in this race last season. Very unlucky in defeat tbf. Beaten just a neck by the winner Yccs Portocervo. He ran on strongly . Just couldn't bridge the gap with the winner, with that horse getting first run on this fella. 
He also finished a solid 2nd in the Grand Sefton off this exact same mark back in November of last year. Beaten just over 3L by the well handicapped winner King Turgeon. He again ran on strongly. Just couldn't get near the winner. 
He ran well lto. Perhaps found the trip on the short side. Beaten 6L back in 4th place behind Matterhorn. He drops back in grade for this race. I think he can run well in this race again.

The model I run suggests My Girl katie could win this one. My Girl Katie lines up here with the highest RPr of this 8 horse race but has an official ranking that leaves it well treated here. Goes out around this 2m 4f trip carrying the second lowest amount of weight, which is a massive 1 stone 11 lbs lighter than the top weight. Prior form figures of 597-11 which looks good on paper, but 208 days since last run means My Girl Katie will need to run well fresh here to get the job done. Model has issued a 'very lo'w stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Hijo De La Luna has had just three starts over hurdles and makes handicap debut. latest hurdles start showed plenty of promise. Was awkward over last two and will improve. Form line between R S Ambush and todays rival Record Art would see the selection come out on top, making the 5yo good ew value at 16/1. Looks worth an EW double with todays NAP Zoffalee in the 2.40pm
Twice a winner from 3 starts on the all weather snd finished 2nd at Chester on 2nd start on turf. Further improvement still likely and has every chance of going 1 better
Should appreciate the drop in trip after racing over a mile and a quarter a Ripon last time out, being a winner over the extended mile at Nottingham in the race prior to that.

Due respect ran a credible race last time out at Redcar over the same distance and the same ground (good to firm) she is up against similar class horses in this contest although based on times over C&D DUE RESPECT comes out on top. 
Forward going jockey booked.

This horse had four races in just a couple of weeks with his former yard.
He finished with what looked to be an improved effort.
Moving to this new yard may provide the impetus for further improvement and he will not need to be a world beater to win this off bottom weight.

4/5 as a 2yo including 2 Group 1's at Newmarket and though best form is on soft ground has handled fast ground too. Made a pleasing debut for the season when third in the 2000 guineas and if that was a 6f race then probably would of won it so dropping in trip seems the right call. Was only a 1/2 l behind the now new superstar Field Of Gold anyway so form is on another level to his rivals here and though yard could of had a better three days at this meeting jockey Willie Buick is getting the big decisions right. Is 3/4 over this trip and loves Newmarket's dip so should relish this stiff track and trip and looks the one to beat.

Jonquil might be from Lope De Vega, but I can only see him being competitive here. His run in the French was quite remarkable, as he was in that front pack of horses which went like bullets at the start. This horse managed to finish 2nd, almost beating a top class miler. The rest of that pack became tired quickly and dropped back. So this horse definetly stays, and itlooked like he has some good speed as well.

BIG MOJO brings the recent Ascot fast ground six furlong winning form which can only read well. A progressive three year old sprinter with a noteworthy sire and ace jockey Hollie Doyle rides the straight course at least as well as any other. Value shout.

Went off a well supported 5/4 fav at Chelmsford but disappointed coming in 3rd and didn't show her usual change of speed and ran on one paced. Will come on for that run and obviously needs to improve again but trainer William Haggas excels with this type.
Impressive when landing a Listed race at Chantilly last time. Comes here in top form and could improve further on fast ground. Good each-way chance.
Arabian Dusk won a G2 last July and ended last tern with a G1 third and returned in April with the latest run being a G2 second which I think puts her in with an EW 5P chance
with 5 places up for grabs 40/1 shot lady of the lamp appeals as a good each way shout.she has a bit to find on ratings with the principles here but can improve again for 2 solid wins this year
Strong warrior can go well for the Fahey yard. Strong warrior has won 2 from 3 races and finished in second in other one ,has ground to help today and has won at this trip before.

Backing Diablo Rojo, the promising 3-year-old colt by Pinatubo trained by Raphael Freire, in tomorrow’s prestigious Commonwealth Cup (Group 1, 6f) at Royal Ascot. Ridden by Rossa Ryan, he brings serious upside based on recent performances. He ran well in the Pavilion Stakes trial at Ascot on April 30, finishing a close second behind Big Mojo over 6f??'beaten by just half a length and showing a sharp late burst . Prior to that, he scored nicely at Lingfield in March, winning a 6f novice event comfortably under David Egan .
Stepping up to this elite Group 1 level will be a test, but his recent Ascot trial form suggests he’s not out of his depth. Freire’s colt has shown he handles the track and steps up well to big-race pressure, especially when the trip kicks in. With Rossa Ryan aboard??'a jockey enjoying a solid Royal meeting and known for his strong finishes??'expect him to settle mid-pack before pushing late through the field. At odds around 66/1 with some bookmakers , he offers strong each??'way value and could surprise the market.
FALAKEYAH looks the real deal and perfectly capable of landing a race of this type based on the quality of the runs up to now and the expected progression.
Ran well as a two year old but looked in need of the run when only 8th in the Irish 1000 Guineas at the Curragh. Likely to do a lot better this time and hard to leave out of calculations.

She's undefeated in all of her 3 runs & is steadily progressing after 2 wins on the all weather at Wolverhampton over 7f & Kempton over 8f she then won Listed at York over today's trip by 0.5L staying on strongly as the end .

The 3yo was beaten just 2L in the 1000 Guineas last month, seeing the race out well but not quite getting to the front two inside the final furlong. It was just her second career run and her first run after a 7 month break. You could expect some improvement after that effort. She’s had a nice seven week break and is at a decent price for this Group 1.
Disapointed last time but her previous run reads well when travelling much the best in the 1000 Guineas. has to deal with a bad draw but clearly enough ability to win a race like this.

Looking for value in this race, as Falakeyah is the one to beat but too short a price for me. Cathedral could represent each way value. Ahead of the re-opposing Flight when second in the Oh So Sharp Stakes on final start over 7 furlongs at Newmarket last year and that horse is half the price of the selection. Sent off favourite on seasonal reappearance when 4th of 6 but only beat 2 lengths over 7 furlongs at Lingfield last month but will come on for the run and this first crack at a mile could suit.

The Coronation Stakes seems to lack a superstar at this stage, with no Desert Flower, Lake Victoria or last years winner Porta Fortuna lining up. The French horse has a quirk or two and I'm not sure about the ground, and whilst Falakeyah was mightily impressive they were fairly modest horses in behind that day. Simmering has saved her best for quick ground and Ascot, having chased home Fairy Godmother over 6f in the Albany last year before winning a pair of Group races, first here at Ascot and then at Deauville. Put her reappearance behind her when finishing a good 3rd in the 1000 Guineas on fast ground before bombing out behind some of these in the Irish version. Trainer reaches for cheekpieces and if the headgear does its trick, a return to fast ground at Ascot should see her go very close in what looks a below par renewal.
Won a listed race in Ireland nicely 15 days ago will come on for that run and is very strong in the betting market so has to be a bet in these conditions.

Took his chance in the Derby on first attempt over this trip earlier this month, sent off 40-1 and 12th of 18 well beaten but possible the undulating track didn’t suit. Worth another look over this trip being a son of Frankel and the first time blinkers are of interest too.

OPPORTUNITY could be a Wathnan three year old of note. Trainer William Haggas has his string in fine form ahead of this year's meeting and this progressive looking type was unlucky when making his run last start. He looks up to racing in ths Group 2 company and rates the value play.

Another difficult 3yo race difficult to call because they are all likely improves.
For value I select this horse who won last time and the second was not disgraced at ascot yesterday.
Top connections add to the appeal so should at least give us a good race for our money.

Possibilities remain for GREEN STORM, who posted his best effort to date when 7th to Lambourn in the Group 1 Derby at Epsom 2 weeks ago. Jockey Billy Loughnane has won once in two rides (50%) when aboard & Green Storm has placed twice in three runs (67%) on good-to-firm or similar going, winning once (33%). Lively outsider.

There should be more to come from ALMOSH’HER, who continued his upward curve when beating Stressfree in the Jorvik Handicap on stable debut at York 5 weeks ago. Jockey Clifford Lee has won once in one ride (100%) when aboard & Almosh’her has won twice in two runs (100%) over 1 mile 4 furlongs. Every chance.
ETHICAL DIAMOND ran well here last season and has progressed enough over hurdles to suggest a return to the flat, in this sort of competition, could be manageable.

Plenty of promise shown including when not beaten far here last year followed by a very impressive win at Glorious Goodwood during the Summer. Can go well fresh first time out and looks a leading contenfer today.

Lightly raced 4yo. Beaten 3L six weeks ago in a Group 3, tricky track, still holding a chance inside the final furlong. He was beaten by four runners 110+, the winner rated 116 and Group 1 class. He shouldn’t fear these handicap rivals, he looks weighted to run a big race and he is a previous 12f C/D winner.

This is drop down in class from last year when War Rooms ran in the Group 2 King Edward VII Stakes here following on from running at York in the Dante where he was 3rd, he moved from Owen Burrows to Gerard Keane in Ireland earlier this year after being gelded and has since run second twice over 14f beaten only a nose last time by San Salvador at Killarney. First time cheekpieces are applied and he drops back to 12f with Colin Keane on board.

Looked very much like he need the race when a no show at Newmarket but had previously won the Golden Gates here at Ascot in good style and winning comfortably and sent off a strong fav. No reason he won't be involved again.
A 3 tines winner who comes here in good form after 2 wins and 4 frame finishes in 6 starts so far this year. Tough and consistent and looks capable of reaching the frame with 5 places.

SIEGE OF TROY has some sound Listed-class form in America and represents a top Irish trainer with high-profile owners. Plenty lining up in this race can stake a realistic claim , so if punted coming from this yard this useful middle-distance type could be interesting.

Naqeeb has been running some respectable races this season. On reappearance he was a little tired late on, and he's last run was very solid but the track might have not suited. Conditions will be perfect here as they'll go hard which suites his staying abilities. It's tough to win with this horse but he has a strong each-way chance.

My selection has improved no end since joining the Tom Dascombe yard, winning on debut at Bath by an impressive 8.5 lengths, before upped in grade (this level) and finishing a fine looking 4th of 23 in the November handicap at Doncaster last year. Had an all-weather listed run in Dec 3rd of 6 before being put away . Reappeared in a 10f class 2 at Chester when beaten a head after being denied a clear run. Comes from a smaller unfashionable yard and if with another bigger one would be single figure odds for sure.

Looked through this twelve furlong race, with the potential of a low draw paying off, as many high drawn runners will be using plenty of energy to get across to hold a position. Satin from Mrs John Harrington stable with Shane Folley in the saddle could be achieving a leading role from stall two and hopefully Shane Folley can get the pace of the race right and try and stack them up behind with kicking on around the bend, using this as a sling shot to go clear and hold on at the finish for a big run appearing. The mare is by Australia and she was behind Ascending only beaten a neck who won here the other day, form looks hot.

HMS PRESIDENT has a single figure draw which on the round course can just about be overcome. Recent renewals of this race have shown such and Alan King's mature type was runner-up in this race two years ago. He could only realistically be an each-way play with extra places available.
Ex French horse won 4 times over there, ran well on British handicap debut in may when running on 4th, steps up in trip which should suit

4th in this last year, Ethical Diamond looks fairly thrown in again, and Almosh’her intrigues again and has been picked up by Wathnan. They are both short enough in a wild race, and I was happy to have a wild go at Brodure here as a result. She needs to prove she handles the ground, but she ran a sound race behind Rose Jaipur last time. A horse in behind had previously finished 4L off Mont De Soleil who was just a couple of lengths behind 116 rated Junko in a Group 2 recently, so whilst it’s fairly abstract form it does suggest a mark of 97 is workable even if it doesn’t look like it on the face of this one’s form. She’s 80/1, and could go forward from a decent draw in a race that lacks an out and out front runner. She’s got something to prove up in trip, and she could be just genuinely outclassed and finish anywhere, but at her price I’m happy to give her a chance

SEE HECTOR ran no sort of race when beaten by Almosh’her in the Jorvik Handicap at York latest but did run 3rd to Silver Knott in the Group 2 turf Dubai City of Gold Stakes at Meydan prior. Jockey Pat Dobbs has placed once in two rides (50%) when aboard & See Hector has placed once in four runs (25%) on good-to-firm or similar going. Lively outsider.

Realign is a horse which would always improve with age, as most horses from Haggas. He probably beat nothing at Salisbury, but he did it nicely and a mark of 93 can't be correct for a horse which wins in such manner. The draw could be a concerning as they came to the stands side on Thursday.

The 3yo filly has 2 wins from 7. She went close earlier in the month in a useful looking class 2 handicap, on good ground. She was coming off a 9 month break and the four runners around her that day were all race fit and all on top of their game. Same mark for this handicap. Improvement likely after that return effort. This fast ground is a positive along with Oisin Murphy taking over in the saddle.

Zayer missed the break at York, but still managed to run a respectable race. The form from that race has worked out well. The fast ground and headgear could make the difference for this runner for connections who won this race 2 years ago.

Top weight HAMMER THE HAMMER has the pace profile and the avoidance of the law draw to potentially get involved here. Considered if keeping vein of the form he arrives in and could still have more to offer.

My selection is dropping considerably in trip having never been over this 5f sprint distance before, but there are some upsides. William Buick takes the ride (tick), with the most competitive side this week being on the stand side (drawn high) stall 31 is another positive (tick) & with the yard in form that's another tick. 6 places on offer also gives me hope.
May have further progression to come following a tough winning display at Chester with the front 2 pulling well clear. Good each way chance with 6 places.

BODHI BEAR representing shrewd Irish connections still a colt has some sort of chance experienced against his own age group. He still has the necessary scope and third-up this spell from a workable mark with a jockey who understands him he is one of many with realistic claims.

Looks a big price for a horse from this yard previously racing with credit in pattern races dropping into this handicap.
Arrives in good form after two good races so far this year so should be sharp enough to place at least.

won in a decent time at epsom with Warren Fentimen taking off a valuable 5f as today in 28 runner sprints you need a jockey with balance and ability but most of all you need luck because race 5 times unless you have a group 1 performer hidden there you have

Brosay has been drifting up the handicap without winning after three 2nd places in his last four races. He finished near the rear as a two year old at Royal Ascot on good to firm but may have been down to his draw and should do better from a high draw this time having changed stables to Paul Attwater in December.

This 3 year old achieved dual victories over 5f from the front last summer and has proven to be even better this term, finishing 2nd in the Epsom Dash 13 days ago, only getting passed by Stormy Impact in the last 50 yards. Given his lightly raced status for a sprinter, there is significant potential for improvement, making it an excellent choice for an each-way bet at 20/1.

Not won since debut but plenty of very good efforts in defeat, slow start to the season on paper but has shaped better than bare result and conditions here should bring out more improvement. Looks potentially very well treated and great value at such long odds.

King of Light has won two and placed once in this class of race and has finished fourth of fourteen in a class above this. Has form over five furlongs and can go well here at a big each way price with six places on offer.

Made a pleasing return to turf two starts ago at Newbury when finishing in midfield in the Fred Darling Stakes at Newbury. Back down in trip back on the AW in what looked a hot contest and proved disappointing having failed to settle. Can do better back on turf where dropping back to 5f is an interesting move but will be a massive price and is probably playing for minor honours.
Daughter of Sands of Mali who made a striking impression when running away with a big field Curragh maiden on debut last month. Will be surprising if she's not on the premises this afternoon.

Two career runs for the 2yo filly. A nice 3L maiden winner on her debut. She was a close runner-up five weeks ago in a Group 3 and that Irish form is looking very strong now. She should be a player in this Group 2.
Was a winner on debut at Carlisle last month over 5f. Likely to improve for having had that run and should be suited by this longer trip. Holds an each way chance

Won a 6f Maiden at he Curragh last month in a fast time on the clock on second career start showing improvement on first start when 4th to Andab who ran well here earloer in the week. Open to plenty of improvement and looks eacj=h way value.

Tahalel doesn't look to have an obvious chance as he was well beaten first time out by Fitzella, who is one of the favourites for this, but he was given a nice quiet introduction as is often the case with the Richard Hannon horses and they often improve a lot for the experience. He is by Blue Point who's horses have been running out of their skin this week at Ascot with 2 winners and a close second out of 6 runners so far. The other Blue Point Nandita for the Gosdens could be worth a saver.

Made debut at Yarmouth and was expected to run well but looked raw and although came with a positive run on the rail it petered out with the pace coming down the centre of the track. Looked much better when winning a modest maiden and looked like the experience had done her good. Can make further progress here at a each way price and 4 places.

this looks more open than the betting suggests and at 25/1 the irish raider oh cecelia appeals.she stepped up on her first win with an emphatic success at cork last time (form has since been franked) and with more improvement to come she looks great value here

Fairy Oak made her debut at Navan in a 5 furlong race with jockey Jamie Powell and a 25/1 proposition, even so she made an excellent effort and managed to finish 2nd in a field of 12 with an acceptable finish, now they move up to Colin Keane jockey with 18% in her last 14 days, the daughter of A'Ali could be the surprise in this test
Won well on debut despite looking green when hit the front. Sire has won over this course and from a respected connections. Good draw and should run better than its price.

Beaten comfortably on debut in America but the winner had previous race experience and then went on to go well at this very meeting yesterday.
Improvement likely and the booking of Rossa Ryan suggests a big race is expected.
Could be anything much like the rest of those in this field,so at this huge price worth an ew punt.

Signora’s form speaks for itself, but you can tie quite a few of these into it. She could well improve the most, and O’Brien has been mopping up these races all week. That said, it surely can’t go on forever, and enough of these are tied in to take a chance. Green Sense is the obvious one given she beat the Fav last time, but the way she was fading and Signora closing you can easily see that form reversing. Venetian Sun looked like she could well for the home team but she’s short enough, so I’ll chance Magny Cours here who looks a big price. She rallied gamely when headed late last time to get up on debut. She had Closely way behind, and that horse has subsequently finished closer than that behind Havana Anna who was 3rd behind True Love and Gstaad on debut who have won here already, and True Love was behind Lady Ivan who beat Signora. So it’s a stretch of a tie in, but a tie in nonetheless, and I think her price is madness as a result, so I’m in.

Fourth on debut at Bath, third at Chester last month and a winner at Brighton four weeks ago, Senorita Vega has been improving and I am backing a big run from her to challenge for the places in this Albany Stakes.

Made her return following an 8 month absence in a 7f handicap at Goodwood and after encountering traffic problems on more than one occasion did well to finish 2nd. Handicapper has put her up a couple of lbs following that but with the extra furlong a definite bonus is a strong contender especially if getting a clear run.

She has good high draw from stall 23 last 4 renewals have seen high draw winners & also rated between 97-101 so she fits both of these stats . She's been placed at Goodwood in Listed & Chantilly in Group 2 both over 8f last run 18 days ago . E.J.H. has already had a winner at the meeting & W.Buick being booked for the ride another plus point .
Emma Lavelle's grey looked a big improver when easily winning at Goodwood last time & could well step-up for the extra furlong, giving the way she went clear last time.
ALFAREQA looks a solid prospect now handicapping and looks very well bred to progress. A solid each-way play at this price with the extra places
Zgharta has been improving with every run, but still shows signs of greenness. I don't think she really liked Newmarket, and a track like Ascot could only see her improve. A rating of 88 seems fair.
The David Simcock trained Arabian Leopard arrives for this fillies handicap on the back of some impressive form including a good second at Haydock last time out an can go well here off a mark of 81.
Ran on and went third over a mile and a quarter at Goodwood last month and will be suited by the likely fast pace dropping back in trip to a mile.
past distance winner who is still only lightly raced and could still improve, 4th of 6 here at Ascot last time out but not beaten far and could be well in at the weights on that last run

Both of Ryka's two wins have come on good to firm going including first time out this season at Newmarket over a mile up five pounds for that narrow win but she is still on a lowly mark of 82 near the bottom of the handicap and should be in the top six home drawn on the stands side.

this looks one of the most open races of the week and serving with style looks amazing each way value at a massive 50/1.with 6 places up for grabs he might get his own way up front and be hard to peg back

Last autumn, the 3-year-old secured 2 all-weather victories over 8.7f at Wolverhampton. Although she didn't make a mark in 2 all-weather handicaps this spring, the narrative changed when she switched to turf at Sandown last week, where she finished 3rd out of 8. With enticing odds of 100/1 for an each-way bet, ti's important to highlight that trainer Heather Main often seems a profit when entering a single runner at a flat meeting.
Noble Horizon well backed lto beaten by a length in a maiden race conditions should be spot on and fallon should be getting this horse home

Made a fair return at Lingfield over 7f following a 10 month absence and gelding op. That was his handicap debut and was never nearer than at the finish. Should strip fitter for that outing and can reward each way support.
Opening Bat is the one to beat looking over all of its form and the nature of all its races it's hard to look past this horse, short and sweet but should be the one to beat.
Can be inconsistent but did win at Nottingham 3 starts ago. Has run respectably in 2 races since and holds sn each way chancevif finding that form today

Is well bred but disappointed on debut when finishing last of 11 at kempton. Should be better than performance showed and this longer trip may help to spark some improvement. That would give an each way chance

This is a better than average handicap for a Newmarket Friday evening card. The three year old, Tilted Kilt, comes up against some older rivals, and with the allowance can come out on top. He's been running consistently well in higher class handicaps against his own age group, and can put the experience to good use here.
Finished a good 2nd of 8 on debut at Chepstow last month but was withdrawn at Windsor next time when bolting at the start. Has every chance if negotiating the start this time

There was plenty to like about his debut run at Salisbury last month when a close 3nd over 5f. He did best of the unrated horses in that race and kept on well. Seemed ill at ease on the track at Bath last time and the race came quickly after that debut run. Should do better here and can give the likely odds on favourite something to think about.
Yet to win from 7 starts but did finish 2nd at Chester on penultimate start. Has every chance if finding that form today

Two nice wins on all weather over 5f at Class 4 level. Stepped up in class since with two runs at Class 3 on turf over 5f, coming 3/10 and 4/16 respectively. In a weaker race here and can run a very strong race.
Visored for the first time LTO did not have the desired effect when 10 of 10 at Chester last month but conditions tomorrow should really suit her and should welcome dropped mark.

Raced just twice as a two year old, finishing a promising 6th on debut at Doncaster before disappointing on heavy ground at Nottingham on his final start. Been off for nearly 8 months but ran okay last time at Leicester on much quicker ground. Makes handicap debut here and can do a lot better and with his yard going well is an interesting runner.

Made a promising return at Sandown at the end of May when making his handicap debut over a mile off a mark of 82. Finished the race off well to take 5th place late on and racing off the same mark here over the same trip in first time cheekpieces is worth considering.
Is the only one in this field with any experience having finished 3rd of 13 on debut 2 weeks ago. Likely to improve snd looks like the one to beat
Only 3rd reserve so may not get a run but did show some promise when finishing 6th of 14 on debut. Holds an each way chance if getting into this field

JACK THE BACHELOR represents an upwardly-mobile Irish trainer and this expensive enough breeze-up purchase could be interesting on debut pitched in at a realistic level. The market is often the best guide in races of this nature , so he looks worth noting.

This Speightstown colt comes from a dam who was a runner up at to 1 mile when she was 2 years old in the U.S. she is half-sister to the experienced Dubai Honour, who triumphed in the Grand Prix de Saint Cloud and won races up to 1 and half miles. Both the Slattery yard and jockey Sheridan are performing well. Given the generous odds of 100/1, I believe placing an each-way bet on this untested 2-year-old presents a valuable opportunity.

HE'S JUSTAGENT may finally be running over a trip which can see him to best effect. He will clearly have no issues racing from his career-low mark which almost certainly underestimates his true ability and third-up for this campaign he could be ready to score.

Should John McConnell's 4-year-old gelding, SHELBOURNE FLYER, get a cameo off the subs bench (1st Reserve) On the basis of his performance 7 days ago at Fairyhouse, I don't think you could totally write him off - at least not if talking about landing some prize money. This son of HOLY ROMAN EMPEROR was keeping on nicely despite being hampered when switching across, so it's no surprise to see this charge being upped in trip here today. This charge ran a nice race on penultimate - again at Fairyhouse -finishing 5th, 5¼ lengths off, finishing ahead of next-time-out winner (Step Back In Time), and is now dropped 1lb for that.
Whilst I'm sure we can all agree this yard have not been firing as frequently as we have seen in previous years, trainer John McConnell knows the time of day, and it would be foolish to ever dismiss any of his runners. 22/1 looks a decent price. Fingers crossed we get a run.

Mint Man won at Dundalk in December and was placed there on 5 other occasions during the Winter. He returned from a break when beaten less than 2 lengths in 5th at Cork last week. He is dropped 1lb and won't need much improvement to win here

Had finished 3rd on his previous two starts without getting a hard ride but proved disappointing next time at Tipperary when well beaten. Much better back there last time when a close up 3rd of 11. Handicaps will now hopefully see him in a better light and one to keep in mind here making his debut in that sphere.

HAPPY HENRY runs now with the yard in much better form and this four year old has a speedy sire and dam. That bodes well for a return to five furlongs in a turf handicap on quick ground and there is something to like about the prospects of this one.
Not beaten far when runner-up over course and distance last time out and is still 2 lbs below his last winning mark.

FLYING BAY is a well bred type who represents an Irish yard who punt those fancied from their yard. This four year old was a short enough price on his seasional reappearance in a big field competitive handicap and sharper now he could be ready to land some bets.
3 time distance winner but well beaten last time over shorter trip, looks to be on a good mark today, will come from off the pace late on

Currently waiting in the wings in the 3rd reserve spot, there is a high possibility that Thomas Coyle's 7-year-old gelding, RUN FORREST RUN, doesn't even get into this contest, BUT at current 33/1 odds I don't want to potentially miss out (no matter how slim the chances of an appearance). This son of BOBBY'S KITTEN knows where the finish line is, and whilst you could argue (and I'd agree) that this charge's preferred trip is 6f, he does have 2 victories over this trip (7f) and was only beaten ¾ of a length here in Northern Ireland on his penultimate start.
To be fair, his run in deeper company at the Curragh 16 days ago wasn't awful - just 5 lengths off the winner. The trainer has a 50% place strike rate here over the past 5 years (albeit from a small sample size), and should his lad nick a spare ride, it wouldn't be a huge shock to see him land some prize money dropping back down in class.

RAZZAM is a five year old who could show the benefit of a switch of yards. This is his second start for new Irish connections and he would have highly likely needed his reappearance sighter. Nothing to fear racing from a mark this low and one worth a glance in the market with a talented claiming apprentice booked.
